- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and recent price is trending upward; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for such cases.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per sentiment-neutral day.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, if last 3 days show strong upward momentum, model often overfits; reduce final 3–5 days by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
